After a slow start, an early surprise followed lounge space. Incident Report for Companion Animal Travel Desk. The desk shift began routine enough, with travelers checking in for pet travel guidance and carrier review before departure. A small issue came up when a pet owner arrived with a carrier that looked sound at first glance but gave off a strong odor and had loose bedding that could shift during handling. The traveler was calm, but the situation needed quick attention because the animal was already in the lounge area and other passengers were nearby.

I moved the traveler aside for a quiet review and asked for a basic check of the carrier latch, airflow, and interior padding. The senior coordinator was notified at once, and we kept the tone steady so the pet would stay settled. The pet, Teddy, stayed inside while we confirmed that the carrier was secure but not ready for immediate acceptance in its current state. The owner was told in plain words that safety comes first and that the desk could not clear the setup until the bedding was replaced and the interior was cleaned. Another staff member fetched approved supplies from the support cabinet, and the carrier was refreshed on the spot.

Once the carrier was cleaned, the odor was reduced, and the bedding was corrected, the pet was rechecked for comfort and calm behavior. The traveler received clear guidance on where to wait and how to keep the animal settled before boarding. No spill, injury, or public disruption followed, and the lounge space returned to normal after the review. The handling was logged for later follow-up, and the coordinator asked for a reminder to be issued to front-line staff about checking scent, latch condition, and bedding stability earlier in the process.

Follow-up is still underway. The Companion Animal Travel Desk will keep a closer eye on carrier condition during intake and will reinforce the same safety-first standard with all travelers. The matter was handled without escalation, and the pet was cleared to continue after the correction. Companion Animal Travel Desk
